review.note: Approved one by one in define-gate slot G3-07 of the resolution-recipe-eval package (REQ-224 exception (b)); the docs PR carrying the answered slot merged 2026-10-10.

question: I control Kalitas, Traitor of Ghet. My opponent controls Blood Artist and Grizzly Bears, and I cast Murder on their Grizzly Bears. Does Blood Artist trigger, and can my opponent respond before I get my Zombie?

expected.shortAnswer: No and no: the Bears is exiled instead of dying, and the Zombie comes from the same replacement, which doesn't use the stack.
expected.answer: No, and no. Kalitas's ability is a replacement effect, marked by the word "instead" (614.1a). When Murder resolves, Grizzly Bears is exiled instead of being put into the graveyard, so it never dies (700.4), and Blood Artist, which triggers when a creature dies, doesn't trigger. Your Zombie token is created as part of that same modified event, which happens in place of the death (614.6), so nothing goes on the stack and there is no point between the exile and the Zombie where your opponent can respond. They can still respond to Murder itself while it is on the stack.

whyHard: A replacement effect changes the event itself, so nothing dies and nothing triggers, and the replacement's own result never uses the stack.
